critical_code_review_comments: services/orchestrator.py::_run_image_gen() — the defensive init of text_out='' and images_out=[] before the try/except is now explicit at lines 153-154. Good. However, on exception the function returns `(f"[Errore image gen: {e}]", [])`, which means the pre-declared text_out/images_out locals are unused on the error path (the returned tuple literal shadows them). This is intentional and behavior-preserving. Consider a code comment stating 'declared up-front to satisfy linter / pyright even though the exception path returns a new tuple'.

src/components/ResponseCard.jsx — the Markdown key `${i}-${chunk.length}-${chunk.charCodeAt(0)||0}` still contains the index `i`, so it is not a pure content hash (a middle chunk edit that changes only length collides only if two adjacent chunks have identical length AND identical first char). This is more stable than pure index but not truly content-addressed. For very long streamed responses this is fine; if you ever regenerate the whole `parts` array mid-render (streaming re-parses on every token), React may still re-mount code blocks. Consider a djb2 or sum-of-charCodes over first/last 32 chars if you observe flicker.

src/components/CompareCard.jsx — using `r.model_id` as the key is correct as long as the /api/compare backend guarantees model_ids are unique in the results array. Backend uses `[asyncio.create_task(one(m)) for m in model_ids]` and returns them in order, so uniqueness is preserved by the frontend caller passing distinct compareModels. Would break silently if the same model_id ever appears twice; low risk today.

src/components/PromptDock.jsx — file chip key `${name}-${size}-${lastModified||i}` is composite and stable. Good. Fallback to `i` when `lastModified` is 0/undefined (rare on File API) means two files with same name+size uploaded in the same tick could collide but React would still recover.

src/components/Telemetry.jsx — inner variable is now named `res` (was `data`). Cleaner. useEffect uses `let mounted = true` guard on the async load, which correctly avoids setState after unmount. No leak. Recent-row key `${created_at_ts}-${model_id}` is stable enough for a 12-item table.

src/lib/api.js — three timeout constants extracted (DEFAULT/ORCHESTRATE/TRANSCRIBE). The values are hard-coded module-level constants; if you later want to tune them per-env, consider reading from process.env.REACT_APP_*_TIMEOUT_MS. Not blocking.

src/components/SessionsPanel.jsx — the useCallback for load() has an empty deps array, which is correct since it only calls the pure listSessions() import. useEffect deps=[refreshKey, load] is technically fine but since load is stable via useCallback([]) the load dep is redundant; harmless. remove() still awaits deleteSession without a try/catch — an API failure surfaces via axios interceptor toast (verified in iter4). No user-visible regression.
